translations.translatedText: # Thursday 4.11.2021 (radio)
Party support. Supplementary budget. Security of supply centre's mask purchases. Student mental health.
## Party support
![October 2021 party support measurement. The National Coalition continues as the largest party.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-12171920)
Open image viewer
Party support in Yle's survey. Photo: Ilkka Kemppinen / Yle

Yle has again asked Finns which party they support. The most support goes to the National Coalition. Almost 21 per cent of respondents support the National Coalition. The support for the National Coalition has stayed the same.
The second most popular party is the SDP. A little over 18 per cent of respondents support the SDP. The SDP is in government, and it is the party of the prime minister.
The third most popular party is the Finns Party. Almost 18 per cent of respondents support the Finns Party. The support for the Finns Party has risen a little.

The National Coalition and the Finns Party are opposition parties, that is, they are not in government. The support for the SDP, a government party, has fallen. The support for the Centre, also a government party, has fallen too. The support for the Greens, a government party, has risen.
## Supplementary budget
![Hybrid car charging electricity.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_2048,h_1152,x_0,y_0/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-5200855bd8912d46dcd/1540919701)
Open image viewer
More money is proposed for housing companies so that they can build charging points. Photo: Yle / Leo Gammals
The government has made a proposal for the fourth supplementary budget this year, that is, for how state money will be given.

The government proposes 30 million euros of extra funding for the police and 65 million euros of extra funding for the Border Guard. For housing companies the government proposes 2 million more support, so that housing companies can build charging points for electric cars.
10 million euros of extra money will be given for energy renovations of housing companies, if Parliament approves the supplementary budget proposal.
## Security of supply centre's mask purchases
![A Finnair plane brought protective equipment ordered from China to Helsinki-Vantaa airport on 15 April.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11322725)
Open image viewer
Masks were brought to Finland from China. Photo: Petteri Sopanen / Yle
The prosecutor has made a decision on the Security of Supply Centre's mask purchases. The prosecutor has decided that the directors of the Security of Supply Centre will not be charged with a crime.
The Security of Supply Centre bought poor masks to Finland last year. The masks could not be used in hospitals, and there were too few of them.

The prosecutor investigated whether the directors had acted wrongly and broken the law. The criminal suspicion concerned the managing director, the administrative director and a department director of the Security of Supply Centre. The prosecutor has decided that the directors will not be charged with a crime.
## Mental health of university students

![A young woman sits in a dark room where the curtains are closed.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_5568,h_3132,x_0,y_322/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-7275065f7db1b1257a6/1602073854)
Open image viewer
Students have depression and anxiety. Photo: Jorge Gonzalez / Yle
Mental health problems among university students have increased this autumn.
The Student Health Care Foundation says that about 3 300 students sought help for mental health reasons in September. The number is about 1000 more than in one month earlier this year.
Doctors say that students have depression and anxiety. The corona time has perhaps been hard for many students.
